text: A Fabric pipeline is genuinely still a pipeline: activities, control flow, If Condition, ForEach, parameters — everything from Chapters Three and Four maps directly. What's different isn't the thinking, it's several of the real building blocks underneath.

In classic ADF, a dataset was its own reusable object sitting between a linked service and an activity. Fabric drops that layer entirely — connection properties are defined inline, directly inside each activity. This guided five-step wizard replaces choosing a dataset first: choose source, connect, choose destination, connect, review and save.

Three real simplifications worth internalizing. Linked services become Connections, managed through a centralized list rather than tied to one factory resource — though connection properties themselves genuinely don't support the dynamic parameterization ADF linked services could. Publish disappears entirely — you Save to store your work, or Run to save and execute immediately. And ADF's separate debug mode is gone too — there's one mode, and it's always live.

Where classic ADF required exporting and re-importing an ARM template just to duplicate a pipeline, Fabric's Save As does it in one single action — a dev copy, a test variation, or a starting template for something similar, created instantly.
Same orchestration thinking, several real building blocks simplified underneath. Next: OneLake as a Destination — one copy of data, genuinely shared across every Fabric workload that touches it.
